title: Failure Ecosystem Probe Canvas — interactive failure triage prototype
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build an interactive prototype called the 'Failure Ecosystem Probe Canvas' — a single-pane triage surface that surfaces failed requests, retry lineage, error taxonomy, and payload diffs alongside cost/latency impact for each retry attempt. The Canvas is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and product debugging flows in the Console. It should let users: 1) surface a failure via filters, 2) inspect the canonical error class and contributing upstream variants, 3) step through retry attempts with side-by-side payload diffs and KV cache snapshots, 4) view per-retry cost/latency and an impact score, and 5) trigger a hypothesis replay (sandbox replay) or create a rollout rule tied to the model/route. Prototype should validate layout trade-offs: combined timeline vs split panels, lightweight vs full payload streaming, and where to surface rollouts/actions without distracting from triage.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with clickable timeline, retry stepper, and payload diff lens (desktop)
Taxonomy strip that groups root error, transient variants, and external service errors with counts and sample rate
Per-retry panel showing tokens generated, latency, GPU-seconds estimate, and cost delta compared to baseline
Payload diff view supports JSON path highlighting, KV cache toggles, and snapshot time travel
Action bar with 'Replay (sandbox)', 'Create rollout rule', and 'Open in request inspector' — each wired to stubs in prototype
Design spec document (Confluence) with accessibility notes and RTL considerations
Design review feedback items captured and a developer feasibility list produced by eng by handoff
comments: 2025-02-18 - Avery Chen: Initial pitch and whiteboard sketches collected during sync with PM and Eng. Core ideas: combine retry lineage + payload diffs; surface cost delta per retry; keep timeline primary. Asked eng for feasibility on live payload streaming and KV cache snapshots.

2025-02-21 - Rohit Kapoor: Eng feasibility: streaming full payloads for high-volume routes expensive; propose sampling + on-demand full payload fetch. KV cache snapshots are available via existing trace logs but need new instrumentation to attach to request IDs. Marking two backend tasks (ENG-19821, ENG-19822).

2025-02-24 - Maya Thompson: Posted high-fidelity frames to Figma. Chose split layout by default (timeline left, details right) but included compact toggle for side-by-side comparison. Added taxonomy chip designs and hover semantics. Requested accessibility review for color contrast on error severity chips.

2025-02-26 - Priya Desai (PM): Reviewed prototype; requested a lightweight 'cost heatline' overlay on the timeline to quickly highlight retries with disproportionate cost. Also asked for a quick path to create a canary rollout from a selected failed request sample.

2025-02-28 - Eng design review (Rohit Kapoor): Noted kernel: need an API endpoint to return per-retry resource estimate; suggested interim workaround to estimate cost client-side using token counts and known cost profile. Also recommended limiting automatic payload fetch to first 3 retries for heavy traffic.

2025-03-01 - Maya Thompson: Updated prototype to add cost heatline, canary action modal, and a compact payload diff with JSON-path jump links. Preparing handoff packet and developer acceptance checklist. Next: schedule HOF with eng and security for rollout action guardrails.
notes: This ticket focuses on the design/prototype deliverable. Backend work should be split into instrumentation (ENG-19821) and cost estimation API (ENG-19822). The prototype should remain functional with sampled payloads and mock cost metrics for the initial usability study.
next_steps: Finalize Figma prototype and export flows for handoff
Schedule joint design + eng + security HOF to confirm rollout guardrails
Run 3-user usability sessions (SRE, Platform Eng, Product) and capture time-to-resolution metric
Produce handoff artifact with component specs, accessibility checklist, and API contract mockups
